tasks.short: Interpret logistics data to explain service, cost, inventory and supplier performance.

steps.what: Retrieve shipment, stock, supplier and cost records for the analysis period.
Align identifiers, units and dates; investigate missing or conflicting records.
Compare service, cost and inventory trends by lane, supplier and product.
Check suspected causes with dispatchers, warehouse staff and purchasing staff.
Record supported explanations, uncertainties and issues needing further investigation.

tasks.design: Configure supported feeds from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}; add deterministic reconciliation checks and a {BI} dashboard. The analyst resolves flagged records and uses linked evidence to record explanations in the {DOCS}; operational changes remain separate decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identifiers, cut-off dates and metric definitions differed across sources. Connecting them required bespoke work, while operational context remained with local teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors, reusable validation code and AI-assisted coding reduce implementation effort. Trend calculations and drill-down views need no language model.
tasks.still_hard: Late events, changing shipment promises and inconsistent cost allocation can distort apparent performance. Correlation alone cannot establish why a delay occurred.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a genuine process failure from a data issue, and challenge explanations against operational reality.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one lane for root-cause investigation.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling data and more time testing explanations with operations. They can propose investigation priorities; spending and operating-policy rights do not automatically change.

reach.learn: Dispatch cut-offs, capacity constraints and event-code meanings.

evidence.claim: Logistics records, reconciliation rules and performance dashboards can use deterministic processing.
Cross-system extracts and operational context commonly require analyst reconciliation and investigation.
Solely automated decisions with significant effects on individuals require a GDPR Article 22 assessment.

assumptions: The baseline describes a mixed environment with system records, analyst workbooks and operational discussions.
Judgment receives more time than the input time split suggests because explaining causes requires context.
Read access uses supported connectors or scheduled files; custom connectors would cost more.
Build ranges estimate a first usable deployment with shared foundations reused across these tasks.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Employee-level monitoring may require consultation under national rules; aggregate logistics analysis does not establish that requirement by itself.
unknowns: Which sources have reliable shipment identifiers and historical timestamps?
Which metric definitions and promise-date changes are authoritative?
Does the proposed dataset identify individual workers or drivers?
Which access and employee-consultation requirements apply locally?
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration provide the required joins before custom code is built?
Which apparent performance changes survive checks for missing events and changing shipment mix?
new_work: Review unmatched records and material reconciliation failures.
Maintain metric definitions, source mappings and data ownership.
Check whether new operational practices invalidate existing comparisons.

tasks.short: Recommend logistics process changes with evidence, trade-offs and a practical implementation proposal.

steps.what: Review findings and define the process problem and desired outcome.
Develop feasible process alternatives and document their operating assumptions.
Estimate each option's cost, service effect and sensitivity to changing volumes.
Discuss feasibility, service risks and practical constraints with affected operations teams.
Write the recommended change, supporting evidence, pilot plan and success measures.

loop.input: Approved option comparison, improvement brief and attributed feasibility feedback.
loop.output: Draft improvement proposal with evidence references, unresolved assumptions and pilot measures.
loop.check: Copy figures from validated fields; verify references and require analyst review of rationale and commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per proposal; missing evidence returns to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Stakeholder constraints and trade-off explanations vary in free text; a fixed template supplies structure but not their synthesis.

steps.what: Approve, reject or request changes to the proposed operational pilot.

tasks.design: A deterministic comparison tool on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines validated logistics data with explicit cost and service assumptions. A bounded drafting loop prepares an evidence-linked proposal in the {DOCS}; the analyst reviews it, and the supply chain manager authorizes any pilot before the {PROJECT} records delivery work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Options were difficult to compare consistently, and proposal writing repeatedly combined calculations with scattered operational feedback.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable scenario calculations and proposal templates are inexpensive to build. Bounded drafting can combine approved evidence and free-text feedback without controlling operations.
tasks.still_hard: Benefits depend on behaviour, supplier cooperation and implementation quality. Stakeholders may disagree about service priorities or who bears the cost.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which trade-offs are acceptable, detect impractical assumptions and earn support from affected teams.

ambition.what: A reversible logistics pilot proposal with explicit success and stop criteria.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more of the week developing and testing alternatives with operations. They gain a stronger role in proposing pilot scope; the supply chain manager retains approval of expenditure and operating changes.

reach.task: Turn an approved process pilot into a delivery plan.
reach.learn: Dependency planning, benefit measurement and pilot exit criteria.

evidence.claim: Deterministic option comparisons can calculate costs and sensitivities while people choose assumptions and trade-offs.
Source-constrained drafting can reduce proposal preparation, but its benefit and accuracy require local validation.
Transporeon checks carrier invoices against agreed rates, supporting the feasibility of rule-based freight-cost checks.

assumptions: The task ends at a pilot decision; implementation is adjacent work.
The input's high judgment prior is retained: option selection and feasibility discussions remain human.
Build ranges assume the validated dataset and approved source documents are available.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Changes affecting employee monitoring or working arrangements may require consultation under national rules.
Draft generation cannot authorize carrier commitments, staffing changes or expenditure.
unknowns: Who can approve pilots, expenditure and service changes?
Which cost assumptions can be reused across proposals?
Which proposed changes affect staffing, work allocation or employee monitoring?
Are previous pilot results available for comparison?
research_questions: Does a structured template alone save enough writing time to omit the model loop?
Which option assumptions most often fail when tested in live operations?
new_work: Review generated proposals for unsupported benefits and omitted constraints.
Maintain comparison formulas and approved cost assumptions.
Record pilot outcomes and compare them with the original forecast.
Update proposal templates and evaluate drafting quality.

tasks.short: Apply forecasting, simulation and optimization methods to logistics decisions.

steps.what: Define the decision, planning horizon, objectives and operational constraints.
Prepare historical demand, lead times, capacity and cost data for modelling.
Select and fit a forecasting, simulation or optimization method.
Backtest predictions and check feasibility, assumptions and sensitivity against operational experience.
Run agreed volume, capacity and service scenarios and summarize results.
Approve model use and proposed planning parameters for operational planning.

tasks.design: Use suitable configured analytics in the {OPS_SYSTEM} first; fill uncovered methods with versioned calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic jobs prepare data, backtest methods and generate scenarios for the {BI}, while approved planning parameters enter the {OPS_SYSTEM} only after the supply chain manager's decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data preparation, repeatable experiments and operational validation were costly to maintain. Available analytical tools did not encode every local constraint.
tasks.enabler_now: Established forecasting and optimization methods can be packaged with reusable data checks, experiment records and scenario controls. AI-assisted coding reduces the work of building this wrapper; it does not remove model uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Sparse history, structural demand changes and missing constraints can invalidate a technically sound model. Novel decisions still require method selection and validation.
tasks.human_edge: Define a useful objective, recognize unrealistic model behaviour and judge whether evidence supports operational use.

ambition.what: Weekly capacity-buffer decisions using demand and lead-time scenarios.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing assumptions and less time rerunning calculations. They can propose parameter changes with documented validation; approval to alter capacity or service commitments remains with operations management.

reach.task: Adjust a weekly capacity plan using approved planning parameters.
reach.learn: Planning freezes, resource calendars and practical limits on rescheduling.

evidence.claim: ORTEC provides operational route planning, showing that logistics optimization can use established software.
The digest reports an Albert Heijn route-planning deployment handling over 300,000 orders weekly; this is not a local benefit estimate.
Backtesting, sensitivity analysis and deterministic optimization do not require a language-model loop.

assumptions: The current analytical application category in {OTHER} is statistical, simulation or optimization software.
Build ranges cover one defined decision problem, not an entire logistics network.
The deterministic rung for method selection supplies fitting and comparison tools; the analyst still selects the method.
The input's structured-data prior supports deterministic processing; low rule coverage preserves human objective setting and validation.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Worker-level allocation or evaluation requires separate assessment and any consultation required by national rules.
Testing ranges cover working effort; observing a full planning cycle may extend elapsed rollout time.
unknowns: Which decision problem has a measurable outcome and sufficient history?
Which forecasting or optimization functions are already licensed and configured?
Which constraints are absent from recorded operational data?
Will proposed parameters affect individual workers or only aggregate capacity?
Who may approve parameter changes and reverse them?
research_questions: Does the proposed method outperform a simple seasonal or current-planning baseline on held-out periods?
Do recommendations remain feasible during disruptions and peak demand?
Can existing analytical configuration meet the need before custom code is added?
new_work: Monitor forecast error, feasibility failures and changing data distributions.
Maintain constraint definitions and versioned model specifications.
Revalidate methods after material operating changes.
Record parameter approvals, overrides and rollback outcomes.

tasks.short: Prepare recurring reports on logistics service, cost and inventory performance.

steps.what: Export reporting-period shipment, inventory and freight-cost records.
Reconcile reporting totals, resolve duplicates and align reporting cut-offs.
Calculate agreed metrics, period comparisons and target variances.
Assemble charts and tables in the recurring report layout.
Add explanations for material variances and identify unresolved data limitations.
Check the final report and circulate it to the agreed recipients.

tasks.design: Reuse the validated dataset on the {DATA_PLATFORM} to calculate agreed metrics in the {BI} and render a dated report from a configured template. The analyst adds supported explanations, then a release action in the {WORKFLOW} publishes the report to the {DOCS} and sends access links through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring reports relied on manual reconciliation, copying and layout work. Teams lacked a shared reporting cut-off and a maintained metric definition.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured data refresh, report rendering and approval flows already cover much of the task. Small deterministic checks can bridge the remaining gaps without a language model.
tasks.still_hard: A polished report can conceal incomplete records or inconsistent definitions. Explaining business causes still depends on validated operational findings.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether a variance deserves attention and ensure the commentary states only what the evidence supports.

ambition.what: A lane-level service and cost report for warehouse shift leads.

tasks.altitude: The analyst replaces recurring report assembly with a short exception and release review. They can offer targeted reporting views, but operational decision rights do not automatically change.

reach.task: Resolve missing shipment events before the reporting cut-off.
reach.learn: Event capture practices, stock adjustments and evidence needed to correct records.

evidence.claim: Recurring logistics metrics, report layouts and internal distribution can use configured reporting and deterministic checks.
Manual extracts, reconciliation workbooks and recurring document reports are a plausible mixed-system baseline.
The proposed effort reduction is a design estimate, not a documented deployment result.

assumptions: Reports serve internal recipients and use agreed metric definitions.
Recurring reports dominate this task; bespoke investigations belong to the interpretation task.
The low model-needed prior is retained: factual summaries use templates and causal commentary remains human.
Build ranges assume a reusable validated dataset; building that foundation is estimated in the interpretation task.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Access is limited by reporting purpose; employee-level reporting may trigger consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which recipients need each level of detail?
Which reports are contractual or require a fixed archived format?
What data completeness threshold permits release?
Does reporting expose identifiable worker or driver performance?
Which existing report subscriptions and templates can be reused?
research_questions: Can a configured reporting template replace the current document layout?
Which current report sections lead to decisions and which can be retired?
Can reporting checks detect late records before publication?
new_work: Review reconciliation exceptions and unresolved reporting limitations.
Maintain templates, recipient access and reporting schedules.
Check metric changes against previously published periods.
Correct and clearly supersede reports when late data materially changes results.

role.altitude: The logistics analyst's week shifts from extracting and formatting records toward causal investigation, scenario validation and pilot design. They gain capacity to propose more frequent planning decisions; authority over expenditure, service commitments and operational changes remains explicitly assigned.
reach: Work with dispatchers to investigate departure-window failures.
Help production planning clerks apply validated capacity scenarios.
Support project management specialists in measuring logistics pilots.
Help shipping receiving and inventory clerks resolve event-quality problems.
skills_to_grow: Logistics data definitions, reconciliation and lineage.
Forecast validation, sensitivity analysis and optimization constraints.
Pilot design, benefit measurement and stakeholder negotiation.
Access control, data minimization and assessment of worker-level analytics.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring logistics decision service: trusted performance evidence, tested planning scenarios and small reversible improvement pilots, each with a named operational decision-maker.
